sources.said: Films that derive humor from physical comedy.

sources.title: Slasher films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026584)
sources.basis: LCGFT scope note (the Library of Congress's own definition of the term)
sources.said: Films that feature a psychotic killer who stalks and murders a series of victims, usually with unconventional weapons.

sources.title: slice-of-life, Merriam-Webster Dictionary
sources.said: of, relating to, or marked by the accurate transcription (as into drama) of a segment of actual life experience

sources.title: social realism (British), Collins English Dictionary (Complete & Unabridged, 2012 Digital Edition), via Dictionary.com
sources.said: the use of realist art, literature, etc as a medium for social or political comment

sources.title: Space operas (Motion pictures) (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2019026020)
sources.basis: LCGFT scope note (the Library of Congress's own definition of the term)
sources.said: Large-scale action and adventure films involving space travel.

sources.title: Spaghetti Westerns (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026595)
sources.basis: LCGFT scope note (the Library of Congress's own definition of the term)
sources.said: Western films usually produced or co-produced by Italian companies and filmed in Europe.

sources.title: Splatter films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2012025038)
sources.basis: LCGFT scope note (the Library of Congress's own definition of the term)
sources.said: Films that feature graphic depictions of gore, hard-core violence, and murder.

sources.title: Sports films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026601)
sources.basis: LCGFT record's source citation, quoting: Moving image genre form guide via WWW, July 19, 2007:
sources.said: Fictional work concentrating on how an individual athlete or team, through strength, training, agility, and/or tactics, compete in the often corrupt world of sports.

sources.title: Spy television programs (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026606)
sources.basis: LCGFT record's source citation, quoting: Moving image genre-form guide online, July 30, 2007
sources.said: Fictional work depicting spies and secret agents seeking to uncover or maintain secrets from each other and for one country or for the benefit of another

sources.title: steampunk, Merriam-Webster Dictionary
sources.said: science fiction dealing with 19th-century societies dominated by historical or imagined steam-powered technology

sources.title: Slattery, A., "Systematically Stoned: The Stoner Film as Genre", Screening the Past, issue 46
sources.basis: the article's own statement of the definition, in a peer-reviewed film journal
sources.said: defines the Stoner film as “by, for, and about pot smokers”, specifying, “these are not movies where a lone joint is passed around in a party scene”

sources.title: Superhero films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026621)
sources.basis: LCGFT record's source citation, quoting: Yee, M.M. Moving image materials, 1988
sources.said: Use for fictional genre films and programs in which the protagonist has superhuman powers, often derived from imaginary technology.

sources.title: Surrealist films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026625)
sources.basis: LCGFT scope note (the Library of Congress's own definition of the term)
sources.said: Films that employ symbolism, juxtaposition of unlike objects, dream-like sequences, etc., to allow the viewer's subconscious to make free associations.

sources.title: Survival films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026626)
sources.basis: LCGFT scope note (the Library of Congress's own definition of the term)
sources.said: Films that feature individuals or groups struggling for their lives in a harsh setting.

sources.title: Swashbuckler films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026628)
sources.basis: LCGFT scope note (the Library of Congress's own definition of the term)
sources.said: Films that feature heroic characters in period costume and have swordplay as a central element.

sources.title: Peplum films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026439)
sources.basis: LCGFT scope note (the Library of Congress's own definition of the term)
sources.said: Films that feature mythological, biblical, or invented strongmen as heroes.

sources.title: Sword and Sorcery, The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction (Clute, Langford, Sleight, eds.; entry updated 10 November 2025)
sources.basis: scholarly reference work
sources.said: describing a subgenre of Fantasy embracing adventures with swordplay and Magic

sources.title: techno-thriller, Merriam-Webster Dictionary
sources.said: a thriller whose plot relies on modern technology

sources.title: Teen films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026632)
sources.basis: LCGFT scope note (the Library of Congress's own definition of the term)
sources.said: Films produced especially for a teenage audience (i.e., the general age range of thirteen through eighteen years) and films with teenagers and teen issues as the primary subject.

sources.title: Thrillers (Motion pictures) (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026692)
sources.basis: LCGFT scope note (the Library of Congress's own definition of the term)
sources.said: Films in which the audience is kept on tenterhooks by plots that feature a build-up of suspense, tension, uncertainty, menace, and anxiety.

sources.title: Time-travel films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2018026154)
sources.basis: LCGFT record's source citation, quoting: López, D. Films by genre, ©1993
sources.said: One of the pet subjects of science fiction is to be able to displace oneself in time in order to observe the past or the future

sources.title: tokusatsu, Dictionary.com Unabridged (based on the Random House Unabridged Dictionary)
sources.said: a genre of Japanese live-action film or television featuring action themes and practical effects

sources.title: Tragedies (Drama) (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2014026576)
sources.basis: LCGFT record's source citation, quoting: Baldick, C. The Oxford dictionary of literary terms, 2008
sources.said: A serious play (or, by extension, a novel) representing the disastrous downfall of a central character, the protagonist.

sources.title: Tragicomedies (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2014026577)
sources.basis: LCGFT scope note (the Library of Congress's own definition of the term)
sources.said: Plays that combine elements of both tragedy and comedy.

sources.title: True crime television programs (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026711)
sources.basis: LCGFT scope note (the Library of Congress's own definition of the term)
sources.said: Nonfiction television programs that feature actual footage and reenactments of criminal and police activities.

sources.title: Vampire films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026716)
sources.basis: LCGFT record's source citation, quoting: Yee, M. Moving image materials, 1988
sources.said: Use for fictional genre films and programs which focus on vampires, i.e., the living dead, who subsist on human blood, and who live in coffins by day and rise at night

sources.title: War films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026729)
sources.basis: LCGFT scope note (the Library of Congress's own definition of the term)
sources.said: Films that feature military conflicts.

sources.title: Werewolf films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026733)
sources.basis: LCGFT record's source citation, quoting: Yee, M. Moving image materials, 1988
sources.said: use for fictional genre films and programs which feature humans who change into wolves

sources.title: Western films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026735)
sources.basis: LCGFT scope note (the Library of Congress's own definition of the term)
sources.said: Films that feature the American West during the period of westward expansion.

sources.title: whodunit, Merriam-Webster Dictionary
sources.said: a detective or mystery story presented as a novel, play, or motion picture

sources.title: wuxia, Merriam-Webster Dictionary
sources.said: a genre of film, fiction, games, etc., that incorporates elements of fantasy, Chinese history, and martial arts

sources.title: Gangster films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026290)
sources.basis: LCGFT record's source citation, quoting: López, D. Films by genre, c1993
sources.said: The yakuza-eiga are contemporary Japanese gangster films, a new genre that appeared in 1964 with the film Bakuto/Gambler, acknowledged as being the first genuine yakuza film.

sources.title: Zombie films (Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms, gf2011026749)
sources.basis: LCGFT scope note (the Library of Congress's own definition of the term)
sources.said: Fictional films that feature the reanimation of corpses that prey on human beings.
